copyPanel.formula: V = Length × Width × Height = Base Area × Height (V = l · w · h = B · h)
steps: 1. Identify the length, width, and height of the box

3. Label answer in cubic units (e.g. in³, cm³, ft³)

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Buying Popcorn
revealWordProblem.text:
You go to the movie theater with your family, and your family likes to buy popcorn to snack on during the movie. The theater sells three different-sized boxes of popcorn. Small: width 4 in., $4.50. Medium: width 5 in., $5.75. Large: width 6 in., $7.00. Each box is a rectangular prism, and the length and height of each box grow with the width.
Question: Is this information enough to determine which box has the lowest price per cubic inch? Identify any measurements you still need, and explain how you would use volume and unit rates to compare the boxes. What else would your family need to decide how many boxes to buy?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The widths and prices alone are not enough to calculate the volumes or decide which box gives the most popcorn per dollar. We also need each box's length and height, or a precise rule relating those dimensions to its width. Saying that the dimensions grow does not give that rule. Once those measurements are available, compute V = length × width × height for each box and compare price ÷ volume in dollars per cubic inch. The number of boxes also depends on how much popcorn the family wants. A complete response identifies the missing measurements and explains this comparison method; it should not invent dimensions or name an unsupported best buy.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
questions.explanation: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: Add 7 + 3 instead of multiplying? Volume uses multiplication of all three edges.
Square inches (in²) measure area, not volume. Volume is cubic (in³).
hints: Notice the three edge lengths: l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in. Volume asks how much space fills the whole box.
Use the volume formula V = l × w × h, and remember volume is measured in cubic units (in³).
Start with 7 × 3 = 21 for the base, then multiply that result by the height, 4 inches.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
questions.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Fíjate en las tres aristas: l = 7 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 4 pulg. El volumen pregunta cuánto espacio llena toda la caja.
Usa la fórmula del volumen V = l × a × h, y recuerda que el volumen se mide en unidades cúbicas (pulg³).
Empieza con 7 × 3 = 21 para la base y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 4 pulgadas.

questions.stem: A time capsule box has a volume of 120 cm³. Its length is 10 cm and width is 4 cm. What is its height?
choiceFeedback: Did you use the formula h = V ÷ (l × w) correctly?
hints: You already know the volume (120 cm³) and two edges (10 cm and 4 cm). The height is the missing piece.
Work backward: since V = l × w × h, divide the volume by the base area (length × width) to find the height.
First find the base area: 10 × 4 = 40 cm². Then figure out what number times 40 gives 120.
questions.stemEs: Una caja de cápsula del tiempo tiene un volumen de 120 cm³. Su largo es 10 cm y su ancho es 4 cm. ¿Cuál es su altura?
hintsEs: Ya conoces el volumen (120 cm³) y dos aristas (10 cm y 4 cm). La altura es la pieza que falta.
Trabaja al revés: como V = l × a × h, divide el volumen entre el área de la base (largo × ancho) para hallar la altura.
Primero halla el área de la base: 10 × 4 = 40 cm². Luego averigua qué número por 40 da 120.

questions.stem: Which unit is used for volume?
questions.explanation: Volume measures 3D space, so it uses cubic units like in³. Square units (in²) are for area, and inches are for length.
choiceFeedback: Square inches measure area (2D), not volume (3D). Volume uses cubic units.
Inches measure length, not volume. Volume is always cubic units.
Degrees measure angles, not volume. Look for cubic units.
hints: Re-read each unit and think dimensions: volume fills 3D space — length, width, AND height.
Match the exponent to the dimensions: 2D area uses square units (²), so 3D volume needs one more dimension.
Picture stacking little cubes inside a box. Each cube is 1 in × 1 in × 1 in — which unit describes a cube like that?
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué unidad se usa para el volumen?
questions.explanationEs: El volumen mide el espacio en tres dimensiones, así que usa unidades cúbicas como in³. Las unidades cuadradas (in²) son para el área y las pulgadas son para la longitud.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer cada unidad y piensa en dimensiones: el volumen llena el espacio 3D — largo, ancho Y altura.
Une el exponente con las dimensiones: el área 2D usa unidades cuadradas (²), así que el volumen 3D necesita una dimensión más.
Imagina apilar cubitos dentro de una caja. Cada cubo mide 1 pulg × 1 pulg × 1 pulg: ¿qué unidad describe un cubo así?

reviewHighlights.formula: V = Length × Width × Height = Base Area × Height (V = l · w · h = B · h)
steps: 1. Identify the length, width, and height of the box
2. Multiply base area (l × w) by height (h)
3. Label answer in cubic units (e.g. in³, cm³, ft³)
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Volume with Whole Number Edges is multiplying only two of the three edges and stopping there — for example, seeing a box that is 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 3 in tall, multiplying just 6 × 4 = 24, and calling that the volume, when 24 is only the area of the bottom face (in square inches), not the volume of the whole box. The height must also be multiplied in: V = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic inches. A second common mistake is adding the three edges instead of multiplying them (6 + 4 + 3 = 13 instead of 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic inches). Volume always MULTIPLIES all three edges, and the answer is always labeled in cubic units (in³), never square units (in²) or plain units (in).

level1.stem: A box is 2 units long, 2 units wide, and 3 units tall. Find its volume.
level1.stemEs: Una caja mide 2 unidades de largo, 2 unidades de ancho y 3 unidades de alto. Halla su volumen.
hints: Count the cubes in one layer. Then multiply by the layers.
hintsEs: Cuenta los cubos de una capa. Luego multiplica por las capas.
level1.explanation: Multiply the length by the width: 2 × 2 = 4 Multiply by the height: 4 × 3 = 12
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica el largo por el ancho: 2 × 2 = 4 Multiplica por la altura: 4 × 3 = 12

level1.stem: A box is 10 in long, 6 in wide, and 4 in tall. Find its volume.
level1.stemEs: Una caja mide 10 pulg de largo, 6 pulg de ancho y 4 pulg de alto. Halla su volumen.

level2.stem: Mo says a box 6 cm long, 2 cm wide, and 3 cm tall has a volume of 11 cubic centimeters, because 6 + 2 + 3 = 11. What is the correct volume?
level2.stemEs: Mo dice que una caja de 6 cm de largo, 2 cm de ancho y 3 cm de alto tiene un volumen de 11 centímetros cúbicos, porque 6 + 2 + 3 = 11. ¿Cuál es el volumen correcto?
hints: Mo added the edges. How do you find the number of cubes?
hintsEs: Mo sumó las aristas. ¿Cómo hallas el número de cubos?
level2.explanation: Multiply the length by the width: 6 × 2 = 12 Multiply by the height: 12 × 3 = 36
level2.explanationEs: Multiplica el largo por el ancho: 6 × 2 = 12 Multiplica por la altura: 12 × 3 = 36

level2.stem: A box has a base area of 35 square centimeters. Its height is 6 cm. Find its volume.
level2.stemEs: Una caja tiene un área de la base de 35 centímetros cuadrados. Su altura mide 6 cm. Halla su volumen.

hintsEs: Volumen = área de la base × altura. Ya conoces el área de la base.
level2.explanation: Write the formula with the base area: V = 35 × 6 Multiply: 35 × 6 = 210
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la fórmula con el área de la base: V = 35 × 6 Multiplica: 35 × 6 = 210

level2.stem: A box is 8 ft long, 3 ft wide, and 2 ft tall. Find its volume.

hints: Multiply the length by the width. Then multiply by the height.
hintsEs: Multiplica el largo por el ancho. Luego multiplica por la altura.
level2.explanation: Multiply the length by the width: 8 × 3 = 24 Multiply by the height: 24 × 2 = 48
level2.explanationEs: Multiplica el largo por el ancho: 8 × 3 = 24 Multiplica por la altura: 24 × 2 = 48

level2.stem: A box is 2 ft long, 5 ft wide, and 3 ft tall. You double only the height. What is the new volume?
level2.stemEs: Una caja mide 2 pies de largo, 5 pies de ancho y 3 pies de alto. Duplicas solo la altura. ¿Cuál es el volumen nuevo?
hints: Find the new height first. Then use length × width × height.
hintsEs: Primero halla la altura nueva. Luego usa largo × ancho × altura.
level2.explanation: Find the new height: 3 × 2 = 6 Find the new volume: 2 × 5 × 6 = 60
level2.explanationEs: Halla la altura nueva: 3 × 2 = 6 Halla el volumen nuevo: 2 × 5 × 6 = 60

level2.stem: A fish tank is 20 inches long, 10 inches wide, and 12 inches tall. How many cubic inches of water fill it?
level2.stemEs: Una pecera mide 20 pulgadas de largo, 10 pulgadas de ancho y 12 pulgadas de alto. ¿Cuántas pulgadas cúbicas de agua la llenan?
hints: The water fills the whole tank. Find the volume of the tank.
hintsEs: El agua llena toda la pecera. Halla el volumen de la pecera.
level2.explanation: Multiply the length by the width: 20 × 10 = 200 Multiply by the height: 200 × 12 = 2,400
level2.explanationEs: Multiplica el largo por el ancho: 20 × 10 = 200 Multiplica por la altura: 200 × 12 = 2,400

level3.stem: A rectangular time capsule container measures 8 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 3 inches tall. What is its volume?
choiceFeedback: That adds 8, 5 and 3. Volume multiplies the three measurements.
That is 8 times 5, the base alone. Multiply by the height of 3 as well.
That is the SURFACE AREA of the six faces, in square inches. Volume multiplies 8 by 5 by 3.
level3.explanation: V = l × w × h = 8 × 5 × 3 = 120 cubic inches.

level3.stem: Box A is 8 in by 5 in by 3 in. Box B is 6 in by 4 in by 5 in. Which box holds more?
level3.stemEs: La caja A mide 8 pulg por 5 pulg por 3 pulg. La caja B mide 6 pulg por 4 pulg por 5 pulg. ¿Qué caja tiene más capacidad?
hints: Do not judge by one edge. Find both volumes.
hintsEs: No juzgues por una sola arista. Halla los dos volúmenes.
level3.explanation: Find the volume of box A: 8 × 5 × 3 = 120 Find the volume of box B: 6 × 4 × 5 = 120
level3.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de la caja A: 8 × 5 × 3 = 120 Halla el volumen de la caja B: 6 × 4 × 5 = 120
choiceFeedback: Box A has the longest edge, but 8 × 5 × 3 = 120, the same as box B.
Box B is the tallest, but 6 × 4 × 5 = 120, the same as box A.

level3.stem: A box has a volume of 105 cubic inches. It is 7 inches long and 5 inches wide. How tall is it?
level3.stemEs: Una caja tiene un volumen de 105 pulgadas cúbicas. Mide 7 pulgadas de largo y 5 pulgadas de ancho. ¿Qué altura tiene?
hints: Find the base area. Then divide the volume by it.
hintsEs: Halla el área de la base. Luego divide el volumen entre ella.
level3.explanation: Find the area of the base: 7 × 5 = 35 Divide the volume by the base area: 105 ÷ 35 = 3
level3.explanationEs: Halla el área de la base: 7 × 5 = 35 Divide el volumen entre el área de la base: 105 ÷ 35 = 3

level3.stem: A cereal box holds 300 cubic inches. It is 10 inches tall and 2 inches deep. How wide is it?
level3.stemEs: A una caja de cereal le caben 300 pulgadas cúbicas. Mide 10 pulgadas de alto y 2 pulgadas de fondo. ¿Cuánto mide de ancho?
hints: Multiply the two edges you know. Divide the volume by that.
hintsEs: Multiplica las dos aristas que conoces. Divide el volumen entre eso.
level3.explanation: Multiply the two edges you know: 10 × 2 = 20 Divide the volume by that area: 300 ÷ 20 = 15
level3.explanationEs: Multiplica las dos aristas que conoces: 10 × 2 = 20 Divide el volumen entre esa área: 300 ÷ 20 = 15

level3.stem: A box has a square base and a height of 5 cm. Its volume is 180 cubic centimeters. How long is each side of the base?
level3.stemEs: Una caja tiene una base cuadrada y una altura de 5 cm. Su volumen es 180 centímetros cúbicos. ¿Cuánto mide cada lado de la base?
hints: Find the base area first. Then find a number times itself that makes it.
hintsEs: Primero halla el área de la base. Luego halla un número que, multiplicado por sí mismo, la dé.
level3.explanation: Divide the volume by the height: 180 ÷ 5 = 36 Find the side of a square with area 36: 6 × 6 = 36
level3.explanationEs: Divide el volumen entre la altura: 180 ÷ 5 = 36 Halla el lado de un cuadrado de área 36: 6 × 6 = 36
